title: Factor normalization of the specified adic-to-condensed compact-support comparison
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and fix finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $g$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites set $B_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$. Use the complete integral categories $\mathcal I_T(R)$, their strict reduction functors $r_T$, and the derived semilinear-system adjunction $r_T\dashv L_T=R\lim U_T$, with unit $u$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $K\in\mathcal I_X(R)$, and assume all integral inputs and proper/open intermediates used below are in these categories, with compatible etale-origin witnesses and common finite cohomological and Tor bounds for their reductions [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

Put $P_RK=R\lim\mathcal T_f^c(K)$ for the strict reduction-tower compact-support functor [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], and $P_R^0=Rg_{*,B}j_{!,B}$ for the separately derived ringed-site proper/open composite [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction]. Let $\mathcal F=S_gJ_j$ be the corresponding simultaneous semilinear-system functor [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Define the system map
$$b_K:r_Y(P_R^0K)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(r_XK)$$
as the system proper coefficient projection (the counit transpose of pullback/scalar balancing for $B\to A_\bullet$), followed by system open scalar extension with identity open restriction [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Its construction is in the derived category of systems, not a specification by evaluated arrows. Identify $L_Y\mathcal F(r_XK)=P_RK$ by the defining strict tower, and put
$$q_{c,K}=L_Y(b_K)u_{P_R^0K}:P_R^0K\longrightarrow P_RK.$$
Let $J_T:\mathcal I_T(R)[1/t]\simeq\mathcal C_T^c(E)$ be the coefficient-extension equivalence, with its specified pullback and direct-image comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Write $P_D^c=Rg_{*,D}j_{!,D}$ for $D=E,F$, where $F/E$ is finite in $\Omega$ or $F=\Omega$; use the finite-subextension-valued ring $\Omega_T^c$ and the actual module-object categories of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category, prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Put $T_T=F_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus].

Then $q_c$ is invertible and its inverse is the normalized single-compactification integral realization of the proper/open word: expressing integral operations in the $P_R^0$ coordinates through $q_c^{-1}$ gives the actual separately derived proper-image and open-extension units, counits, proper/open interchange and composition maps of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization, lem-sf-integral-compactification-comparison-bridge]. This fixes the integral coordinates used in the following two equalities.

The specified comparison $a_{f,E,K}$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization] is exactly
$$a_{f,E,K}=Rg_{*,E}(\delta^J_{j,K})\circ\chi^J_{g,j_{!,B}K}\circ J_Y(q_{c,K}^{-1}[1/t]).$$
Here $\chi^J_g:J_YRg_{*,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_{*,E}J_Z$ is the direct-image comparison of $J$, after rationalization; $\delta^J_j:J_Zj_{!,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,E}J_X$ is the scalar/open comparison whose restriction to the open is the identity under the balanced tensor identifications, equivalently whose inverse is the open-adjunction adjunct of the open unit [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

Put $K_E=J_X(K[1/t])\in\mathcal C_X^c(E)$. For the same specified compactification, the coefficient projection comparison $\xi_{f,E,F}:T_YP_E^c\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F^cT_X$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization] is exactly
$$\xi_{f,E,F,K_E}=Rg_{*,F}(\delta^{E,F}_{j,K_E})\circ\pi_{g,j_{!,E}K_E}.$$
The open map $\delta^{E,F}_j:T_Zj_{!,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,F}T_X$ is again identity on the open under scalar balancing. The proper map $\pi_{g,L}:T_YRg_{*,E}L\to Rg_{*,F}T_ZL$ is the $Lg_F^*\dashv Rg_{*,F}$-adjunct of the specific composite
$$Lg_F^*T_YRg_{*,E}L\xrightarrow{\mu}T_ZLg_E^*Rg_{*,E}L\xrightarrow{T_Z\varepsilon_{g,E,L}}T_ZL,$$
where $\mu$ is canonical pullback/tensor balancing. This formula also holds for $F=\Omega$, as an equality in the $F^c$-module derived category, and $\pi_g$ is invertible on the stated domain. For an identity open $j$, both displayed compact-support comparisons reduce to their specified proper factors, with the identity open factor. The displayed maps are natural in $K$; no endomorphism, equality of proper-unit compact-support operators, or point realization is asserted.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6, Lemma 6.7.14, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15 give the compactification and coefficient context only. Agent-formulated normalization of the specified comparison maps of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, whose proof Steps 2–5, 6 and 13 motivate the formulas; not an assertion literally stated by Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: Write $D=j_{!,B}K$ and $N=S_gJ_jr_XK$. All complete inputs and intermediate bounds are supplied by the hypotheses. The coefficient identifications for $B_T$ and $(A_n)_T$ commute with quotient maps by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] to $g$ and $D$: the proper factor of $b$ is its specified diagram-site projection mate. Its evaluations are isomorphisms, since $D$ is complete. The coefficient hypotheses hold: $R$ is a Noetherian DVR and $A_n$ is finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ resolves $A_n$ by finite free modules. The second factor is the strict open reduction isomorphism $r_j:r_ZD\to J_jr_XK$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Thus $b=S_g(r_j)r_g$ is a system map and is invertible, using detection of isomorphisms in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The strict-tower definition [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] identifies $\mathcal L_YN=P_RK$ with its prescribed transitions and maps. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies the actual quotient-tower unit with the completion unit; it is invertible on $P_R^0K$, which is complete by hypothesis. Therefore $q=\mathcal L(b)u_{P_R^0K}$ is invertible.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.14 (context); agent verification using the cited strict-system and completion statements

proof.text:
Let $d_g:\mathcal L_YS_gr_ZD\to Rg_{*,B}D$ be the specified one-letter identification and $e$ the system counit. The basic transpose formula of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence] says $r_g=e_{S_gr_ZD}r_Y(d_g^{-1})$. Naturality of the actual unit and its triangle identity [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] give
$$
\mathcal L_Y(r_g)u_{Rg_{*,B}D}
=\mathcal L_Y(e_{S_gr_ZD})u_{\mathcal L_YS_gr_ZD}d_g^{-1}=d_g^{-1}.
$$
Consequently
$$q=\mathcal L_YS_g(r_j)d_g^{-1},\qquad q^{-1}=d_g\,\mathcal L_YS_g(r_j^{-1}).$$
This also gives $e_Nr_Y(q)=b$: substitute $q=\mathcal L(b)u$, move $b$ past $e$ by naturality, and cancel $e_{r_Y(P_R^0K)}r_Y(u)=1$. These are equations in the derived system adjunction, with the specified unit, rather than equations inferred from evaluated arrows.

source.place: Tensor reassociation and adjunction units/counits sentence; explicit two-letter transpose cancellation

proof.text:
Check the structural normalization before using these coordinates. For a generator $\tau:B\to C$, let $r_B,r_C$ be the successive proper/open coefficient comparisons. The generator theorem [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence] gives $\tau r_B=r_Cr(\tau_{\rm int})$ inside the system category. Put $q_B=\mathcal L(r_B)u$ and similarly for $C$. Apply $\mathcal L$ and use naturality of $u$ to obtain
$$\mathcal L(\tau)q_B=q_C\tau_{\rm int}.$$
Thus conjugation by the inverse comparisons gives precisely the separately derived units, counits, proper/open interchange and compositors. For the two-letter word $S_gJ_j$, $r_B=b$, so this comparison is exactly the $q$ of Step 2. For basic proper and open letters this uses the stated $d_g$ and the open comparison $d_j=u_D^{-1}\mathcal L(r_j)^{-1}$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. The expression-realization theorem [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] supplies the realization for all allowed contexts and its intertwining of these same generators. On a composite of generator arrows the adjacent inverse comparisons cancel. Hence this verification compares actual structural maps, including their whiskerings, on the assumed domain.

source.place: Generator comparisons and coherence; explicit conjugation of the strict-system generator square

proof.text:
Check the completed compactification composition with the precise bridge [lem-sf-integral-compactification-comparison-bridge]. Identify each $F_v$ there with $P_{R,v}=\mathcal LB_vr$ by its direct defining-tower identification $d_v$; these identifications are retained on morphisms. The bridge then reads
$$\alpha_{g,f}=\mathcal L(\beta)\,\mathcal LB_g(e_{B_frK})$$
with source $\mathcal LB_gr(\mathcal LB_frK)$. For separately derived word coordinates put
$$Q_{g,f}=\mathcal LB_g(e_{B_frK})\,q_{g,P_{R,f}K}\,P_{R,g}^0(q_{f,K}).$$
It maps $P_{R,g}^0P_{R,f}^0K$ to $\mathcal LB_gB_frK$. This is the successive word comparison: substitute $q_f=\mathcal L(b_f)u$ and $q_g=\mathcal L(b_g)u$, move $b_f$ past $e$ by naturality, and cancel $e_{rM}r(u_M)=1$. The result is precisely $\mathcal L(r_{B_gB_f})u$, where $r_{B_gB_f}$ is the composite of the proper/open letter comparisons. The triangles used here are those of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The generator squares of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], applied successively to the proper/open interchange and compositors forming $\beta$, give by Step 3
$$q_h^{-1}\mathcal L(\beta)Q_{g,f}=\beta_{\rm int}.$$
Substitution of the bridge formula is the required equality for the specified completed composition. Thus the comparison is with that composition, with its inserted counit, and the same separately derived proper/open maps. No arbitrary expression-realization is substituted for the bridge's direct $d_v$.

source.place: Step 5; application of the existing actual-map comparison bridge

proof.text:
Now expand the specification of $a_{f,E}$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], construction Steps 3--5. It first inverts $\mathcal L(b)u$, then applies coefficient realization to the separately derived proper/open word. The first arrow is therefore $J_Y(q^{-1}[1/t])$, by Step 2. Its proper arrow is exactly $\chi_g^J$: [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] specifies $J$ as derived coefficient extension and fixes its direct-image comparison, including counits. Its open arrow is $\delta_j^J$: apply [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to the identity of $Z$ with coefficient map $B_Z\to E_Z^c$; its restriction is identity under balancing and its inverse is the specified open-unit adjunct. This identifies each arrow in the defining ordered composite, rather than replacing it by another isomorphism between the same objects. Associating these three arrows yields
$$a_{f,E,K}=Rg_{*,E}(\delta^J_{j,K})\,\chi^J_{g,j_{!,B}K}\,J_Y(q^{-1}_{c,K}[1/t]).$$

source.place: Agent-formulated specified-map construction of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, Steps 3--5; Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15 give context, not this formula

proof.text: For finite $F/E$, [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] gives finite freeness of $F_Y^c$ over $E_Y^c$. The inverse-image coefficient identifications are the composition identifications of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Apply [lem-sp-finite-free-direct-image-coherence] with $q=g$, coefficient rings $E^c,F^c$, and $L=j_{!,E}K_E$. Its specified isomorphism $\pi_g$ is the adjunct of $T_Z(\varepsilon_{g,E,L})\mu$, exactly the proper map in the question; in particular it is a map of $F^c$-modules. Apply [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to scalar extension $E_Z^c\to F_Z^c$ for $j$. This supplies $\delta_j^{E,F}$ with identity open restriction. Expanding the canonical coefficient projection of the composite $P_E^c=Rg_{*,E}j_{!,E}$, its first arrow is $\pi_{g,j_{!,E}K_E}$ and its second is $Rg_{*,F}(\delta_j^{E,F})$. This is the specification used for $\xi$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], construction Step 6. It proves the second displayed equality for finite $F$, including invertibility of its proper factor.

source.place: Agent-formulated finite coefficient comparison, construction Step 6 of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization; Remark 6.8.15 is context

proof.text: For $F=\Omega$, use the small filtered poset of finite $H\subset\Omega$ containing $E$, final among finite intermediate fields by composita. The coefficient ring and scalar cocone are those of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit], so they consist of finite-subextension-valued functions. Put $L=j_{!,E}K_E$, bounded below. The presentation theorem [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-coefficient-complex-presentation], with its base field and input field both $E$, gives simultaneous representatives of $T_{E,H}L$ with one common lower bound and identifies the coefficient cocone maps under transposition. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] scalar extension is exact, so the bound is retained. The proper $g$ is qcqs. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] with coefficient sheaf $E^c$: the colimit of the restricted finite proper comparisons is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. The restriction/direct-image comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identifies its target with the restriction of $Rg_{*,\Omega}T_{E,\Omega}L$ and reflects isomorphisms. The resulting map is the restriction of the actual $\Omega^c$-linear adjunct $\pi_g$ of $T_Z(\varepsilon)\mu$. Indeed on each finite cocone leg its transpose is the same balanced pullback followed by the same counit; the presentation theorem's transposition identity identifies these with the colimit legs. Thus $\pi_g$ itself is invertible in $D(\Omega_Y^c)$, with exactly the stated mate formula.

source.place: Agent verification of the algebraic-closure coefficient step of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, Step 13; the cited simultaneous presentation and bounded-below continuity supply the precise argument

proof.text:
The open comparison at $E\to\Omega$ is supplied directly by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], for the ring map $E_Z^c\to\Omega_Z^c$. Its inverse is the open-unit adjunct, so restriction to $X$ is the balanced identity. Exact open extension is a left adjoint by the same statement's open adjunction; hence it commutes with the coefficient colimit. On every finite cocone leg the composite $Rg_{*,\Omega}(\delta_j^{E,\Omega})\pi_g$ is the scalar-extended composite of Step 6: proper coefficient transitivity is [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle], and open transitivity follows by taking adjuncts, where both maps are identity after balancing. The simultaneous presentation identifies these actual cocone arrows, not just objects. The definition of $\xi_{f,E,\Omega}$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], construction Step 13, is the same colimit coefficient projection. The cocone equations therefore give
$$\xi_{f,E,\Omega,K_E}=Rg_{*,\Omega}(\delta^{E,\Omega}_{j,K_E})\,\pi_{g,j_{!,E}K_E}$$
in the $\Omega^c$-module derived category. This uses a colimit cocone of representing complexes with a common lower bound; no faithfulness of finite evaluation or unrestricted derived colimit assertion is needed.

source.place: Agent verification of the specified algebraic-closure coefficient projection, construction Step 13; open-unit normalization and coefficient transitivity

proof.text: All factors are natural transformations: $u$, the strict coefficient maps, their inverses on this domain, the direct-image comparison of $J$, and the scalar/open adjunction comparisons. Applying the preceding composites to a morphism $K\to K'$ therefore gives their naturality squares. If $j=\mathrm{id}$, its unit is identity; [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] gives $r_j=1$ and both $\delta_j=1$ under the coefficient unitors. Step 2 then reads $q^{-1}=d_g$, and the first compact-support formula is precisely the specified proper realization comparison; the second is $\pi_g$. If also $g=\mathrm{id}$, $q=u_K$ and its inverse is the completion identification, as the same triangle calculation shows. For $K=0$ or an empty open all proper/open images are zero and all displayed comparisons are the unique maps between zero objects. For $F=E$, coefficient transitivity's identity clause makes $\pi_g$ and the scalar/open factor identity. None of these checks adds a nonzero, nonempty, or positive-rank hypothesis.
